potential_name: Purja Pun and Mishin (2009) Ni-Al EAM
authors: G. P. Purja Pun and Y. Mishin
citation: G. P. Purja Pun and Y. Mishin (2009), 'Development of an interatomic potential for the Ni-Al system', Philosophical Magazine 89(34-36), 3245-3267.
fitting_emphasis: Binary Ni-Al potential built on established pure Al and pure Ni descriptions; cross interaction fitted to experimental cohesive energy, lattice parameter, and elastic constants of B2-NiAl plus ab initio formation energies of several real or hypothetical intermetallic compounds; intended for Ni-Al phases, heterophase interfaces, and mechanical behavior.

citation: Y. Mishin (2004), 'Atomistic modeling of the gamma and gamma'-phases of the Ni-Al system', Acta Materialia 52(6), 1451-1467.
fitting_emphasis: Ni-Al potential developed primarily for the gamma (Ni solid solution) and gamma-prime (Ni3Al) phases; fitted to experimental and first-principles data for lattice properties, point defects, planar faults, and phase-diagram characteristics; narrower intended composition scope than the 2009 general binary potential.
known_implementation_warnings: The superseded ipr1 implementation (NiAl.eam.alloy) must not be used; it has non-zero isolated-atom energies.
superseded_status: uses corrected ipr2; superseded ipr1 rejected

potential_name: Mishin, Mehl, and Papaconstantopoulos (2002) B2-NiAl EAM
authors: Y. Mishin, M. J. Mehl, and D. A. Papaconstantopoulos
citation: Y. Mishin, M. J. Mehl, and D. A. Papaconstantopoulos (2002), 'Embedded-atom potential for B2-NiAl', Physical Review B 65(22), 224114.
fitting_emphasis: Historical EAM optimized for the B2 phase of NiAl, fitted to experimental properties and ab initio data for multiple crystal structures; accurately reproduces basic B2-NiAl lattice properties, planar faults, and point-defect characteristics.
known_implementation_warnings: NIST documentation cautions that the elemental descriptions taken from this B2-optimized alloy fit may perform poorly for pure Ni, pure Al, and non-B2 Ni-Al phases; this directly affects formation-energy transferability across the five selected compositions.
